name: Euro-area economy
value: Q3 GDP +0.4%; Oct composite PMI above 50
summary: Euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3 and the October composite PMI stayed above 50; November flash PMIs not yet out
state: Eurostat confirmed euro-area GDP growth of 0.4% in the third quarter in its estimate of 13 Nov (Eurostat; RTTNews). The HCOB flash composite PMI fell to a four-month low of 51.9 in October from September, below forecasts but still above 50 (FXStreet, 23 Oct). November flash PMIs had not been published as of 19 Nov, so the latest data remain consistent with Normal.
for_you: Growth in the euro area is positive but slowing, which matters for UK exporters to Europe and for jobs in trade-exposed sectors. Higher borrowing costs remain the main pressure on households and firms.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% (positive) and October composite PMI above 50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
RTTNews — Eurozone GDP growth confirmed at 0.4%
FXStreet — Eurozone HCOB Composite PMI declines to 51.9 in October vs 52.7 expected

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
